annotation.evidence_span: A TCP MUST be able to receive a TCP option in any segment.
annotation.interpretation_a: A TCP implementation must allocate resources to parse *any* valid TCP option, even if it will ultimately discard the information. This implies a potentially unbounded memory allocation requirement.
annotation.interpretation_b: A TCP implementation only needs to be able to receive a TCP option if it *supports* that option. It can silently drop or error on unknown options without violating this requirement.
annotation.justification: The verb 'able to receive' is ambiguous. It could mean 'capable of accepting the bytes' or 'capable of fully processing the option'. Without further clarification, implementations could reasonably choose different approaches to handling unknown options, leading to interoperability issues.
annotation.missing_information: The clause does not specify whether the TCP implementation must be able to *process* any TCP option, or merely *receive* the bytes representing the option. The difference affects resource allocation and error handling.
